entities.summary: James Alexander Walker was an American lawyer, politician, and Confederate general during the American Civil War, later serving as a United States Congressman for two terms. He earned the nickname "Stonewall Jim" for his days as commander of the famed Stonewall Brigade. Walker is the first graduate of the Virginia Military Institute to serve as Lieutenant Governor of Virginia. He was expelled from the Institute weeks before graduation in 1852 amidst a bitter dispute with then-mathematics professor Thomas Jackson, but was granted his degree in 1872 in recognition of his military service in the American Civil War.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent Confederate general and politician, James A. Walker played a significant role in shaping the course of the American Civil War. His leadership as commander of the Stonewall Brigade had far-reaching consequences for the Confederacy's military strategy.
